title: Module right adjoint for a qcqs morphism of algebraic stacks
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Use their big fppf sites and structure sheaves from [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], module sheaves from [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and quasi-coherent modules meaning modules locally presented by small sums of the structure sheaf. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Tensor pullback, which agrees with precomposition on these quasi-coherent module sheaves [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], has a right adjoint $R_f:\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal Y)$. Thus there are natural bijections $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal X}(f^*G,F)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal Y}(G,R_fF).$$ There is a natural module map $i_{f,F}:R_fF\to f_*F$, where $(f_*F)(t:T\to\mathcal Y)=\Gamma(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T,F|_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T})$ and restrictions are induced by base change. For a module map $h:G\to R_fF$ with transpose $\bar h:f^*G\to F$, $i_{f,F}h$ is the ordinary module-sheaf adjunct of $\bar h$. No quasi-coherence of the naive big-fppf sheaf $f_*F$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 077A, proposition-direct-image-quasi-coherent, degree-zero adjunction and its proof; the canonical map is the counit of the coherator Q used there.

proof.text: For a quasi-coherent $F$ on $\mathcal X$, its scheme restrictions and all tensor comparison maps are those of [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction]. Thus $F$ is locally quasi-coherent with flat comparison maps. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-higher-images-flat-comparison] in degree zero: $H_F=f_*F$ is locally quasi-coherent and flat-compatible on $\mathcal Y$. Its big-fppf section and restriction formulas are exactly the formulas in the statement. The same restriction lemma ensures that $f^*$ preserves quasi-coherent modules.

source.place: Tag 077A (proposition-direct-image-quasi-coherent), proof, using Tag 0771 (proposition-loc-qcoh-flat-base-change), degree zero.

proof.text: The functor of fibred categories underlying $f$ gives a morphism of ringed fppf topoi with unchanged structure ring by [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image]. Its tensor pullback is precomposition. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to obtain natural bijections $A_{G,F}:\operatorname{Hom}(f^*G,F)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(G,H_F)$ for all module sheaves. For quasi-coherent $G,F$, the first Hom is the Hom in $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal X)$, since this is a full subcategory; the second is the Hom in the full locally quasi-coherent flat-compatible category.

Use [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator] for $\mathcal Y$ and define $R_f(F)=Q_{\mathcal Y}(H_F)$, acting on morphisms by $Q_{\mathcal Y}(f_*(-))$. Its counit bijection $B_{G,H}:\operatorname{Hom}(G,Q_{\mathcal Y}H)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)$ is $h\mapsto q_Hh$. Therefore $B_{G,H_F}^{-1}A_{G,F}$ is the required natural Hom bijection, proving $f^*\dashv R_f$. Put $i_{f,F}=q_{H_F}:R_fF\to f_*F$; this is a module map natural in $F$.

If $h:G\to R_fF$ has transpose $\bar h$, the definition of the composed bijection says $h=B_{G,H_F}^{-1}(A_{G,F}(\bar h))$. Applying $B$ gives $i_{f,F}h=q_{H_F}h=A_{G,F}(\bar h)$, which is precisely the ordinary module-sheaf adjunct of $\bar h$. This uses the counit formula in [lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator] and the ordinary bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q53-129593450 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: no repairs and no fixes/ files. The item statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical to the Q125 snapshot where the item was created, so no target was weakened. There is no repair note for this item, so this is not a 2026-10-21 re-split. The split follows the proof of Stacks 077A (stacks-cohomology.tex l.1905). Step 1: lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction makes quasi-coherent F locally quasi-coherent with all comparison maps isomorphisms. lem-sfb-stack-higher-images-flat-comparison (0771) then puts R^0f_*F = f_*F (section formula) in the locally quasi-coherent flat-compatible category, under the same hypotheses: algebraic stacks and f qcqs. Step 2: lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-ringed-inverse-image and lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction (03D7) give the ordinary Hom bijection; its module structure on the direct image is the pullback-of-functions structure. Step 3: the new coherator node gives R_f = Q f_* and i_{f,F} = q at f_*F. Step 4 is a genuine two-line substitution that recovers the transpose formula. One minor point, not counted as a gap: both cited nodes take the section-formula f_* to be the topos pushforward (06TS/06W6). New node lem-sfb-stack-lqc-coherator matches Stacks 0778 (lemma-adjoint, l.1415). It is posed on big-fppf modules instead of etale ones; this is equivalent because objects of LQCoh^fbc are fppf sheaves. Its counit formula is the standard one and Q j = id holds because j is fully faithful. It is statement-only, self-contained, every notion cites a definition node, and it is strictly smaller than the item. Tested on a scheme, on the empty stack and on the punctured plane. Duplicate search: rg -L over the snapshot DAG for 0778, coherator, LQCoh and flat-compatible, and a grep of blueprint main-20261015. Candidates read: lqc-flat-comparison-local-structure, smooth-descent-higher-image-criterion, qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness, flat-module-pushforward-comparison (a citer, consistent with the unchanged item) and pc-dq-coherator (derived, on schemes). None is a duplicate. Accepted tool_use: lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction, the generic 03D7 adjunction. Batch-5 flags: def-trf-algebraic-space and def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module are general definitions. lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence is the general Zariski/etale equivalence of quasi-coherent modules, which neither the trace formula nor Poincare duality gives. All three are accepted. No SGA source is used.
